questions.q: What goal do all forms of socialism share, according to the summary?
a: Creating an egalitarian society
Maximizing national economic growth
Preserving traditional social hierarchies
Keeping government as small as possible
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the common aim is an egalitarian society, though governments disagree on how to reach it.

questions.q: What do socialists agree is the source of society’s inequalities?
a: Capitalism
Human nature
A lack of education
Religious differences
questions.why: Lesson 1 says socialists agree that inequality stems from capitalism, especially elite control of capital.

questions.q: What did socialists disagree about after Marx died?
a: How socialism should be put into practice
Whether capitalism was harmful at all
Whether workers deserved higher wages
Whether classes existed in society
questions.why: Lesson 2 says Marx left open the question of implementation, which split socialists into reformists and revolutionaries.

questions.q: Which approach did the social democrats favor?
a: Reforming capitalism through democratic elections
Overthrowing the bourgeoisie in a violent revolution
Leaving markets entirely free of regulation
Handing factories directly to military leaders
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes social democrats as winning power at the ballot box to help the working class.

questions.q: What does the summary call the most obvious lesson from past socialist experiments?
a: A socialist society must be democratic at every level
Socialism works best with a single strong leader
Markets should never be regulated by the state
Public ownership always lowers living standards
questions.why: Lesson 3 says authoritarian rule cannot be an option and socialism needs democracy at every level.
